Paper: [Girshick et al. (2014), Rich Feature Hierarchies for Accurate Object Detection and Semantic Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.2524).
The preprint first appeared in 2013.

## Problem

Object detection must determine both what objects are present and where they are located.
A whole-image classifier does not directly provide a separate class and bounding box for every object.
R-CNN applies learned CNN features to candidate regions supplied by a proposal method.

## Previous Attempts

Earlier detectors relied heavily on designed features and specialized detection models.
R-CNN combines existing region proposals with CNN features pretrained for image classification and adapted to detection.
Selective search is an input component of the pipeline, not an algorithm introduced by R-CNN. [Sections 1–2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1311.2524#page=2).

## Proposed Solution

Selective search supplies candidate boxes.
Each proposal is cropped from the image and warped to the CNN's fixed input size, then processed separately to obtain a feature vector.
Class-specific linear SVMs score those features, and bounding-box regressors refine the proposal coordinates.
Non-maximum suppression reduces redundant detections. [Section 2 and Figure 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1311.2524#page=2).

Training consists of distinct stages with different positive-example definitions.
The CNN starts from supervised ImageNet pretraining and is fine-tuned with a foreground-plus-background softmax classifier.
For this stage, a proposal overlapping a ground-truth box by at least 0.5 IoU is positive for the matched class.
The subsequent SVM stage uses ground-truth boxes as positives, proposals below 0.3 IoU with that class as negatives, and hard-negative mining.
The overlap thresholds and labeling rules therefore cannot be combined into one universal R-CNN positive/negative test. [Section 2.3 and Appendix B](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1311.2524#page=12).

## Bounding-Box Regression {#box-regression}

Represent a proposal as center coordinates and size, $P=(P_x,P_y,P_w,P_h)$, with target box $G$ in the same form.
The regression targets are normalized center shifts and logarithmic size ratios:

$$
    \begin{aligned}
        t_x&=(G_x-P_x)/P_w,\\
        t_y&=(G_y-P_y)/P_h,\\
        t_w&=\log(G_w/P_w),\\
        t_h&=\log(G_h/P_h).
    \end{aligned}
$$

The original paper fits four linear regressors with squared error and L2 regularization, that is, ridge regression.
It does **not** use the Smooth L1 box objective later introduced in [Fast R-CNN](fast-r-cnn.qmd). [Appendix C, Equation 5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1311.2524#page=12).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false" title="Derivation: decoding shifts and log-scale predictions"}
If the feature-based regressors predict $d_x,d_y,d_w,d_h$, invert the target transformations:

$$
    \begin{aligned}
        \hat G_x&=P_x+P_wd_x,\\
        \hat G_y&=P_y+P_hd_y,\\
        \hat G_w&=P_w e^{d_w},\\
        \hat G_h&=P_h e^{d_h}.
    \end{aligned}
$$

A predicted width shift $d_w=\log 2$ doubles the proposal width.
A zero shift leaves that coordinate unchanged.
Center targets scale displacement relative to the proposal's size, so the same normalized shift has a larger pixel effect for a larger proposal.
:::

## Overlap and Suppression {#iou-nms}

Intersection over union compares box overlap:

$$
    \operatorname{IoU}(A,B)=\frac{|A\cap B|}{|A\cup B|}.
$$

Class-wise non-maximum suppression repeatedly retains a high-scoring box and suppresses sufficiently overlapping lower-scoring boxes.
Several spatially separated detections can remain; the procedure does not reduce the entire image to one proposal.
Its threshold is a suppression choice, distinct from the IoU thresholds used to assign training labels.

## Evidence and Limitations

The paper reports detection improvements from CNN features, supervised pretraining, fine-tuning, and box regression through its benchmark comparisons and ablations. [Section 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1311.2524#page=4).
Repeated CNN evaluation for overlapping regions and separate training stages make this pipeline expensive.
[Fast R-CNN](fast-r-cnn.qmd) shares convolutional features across proposals, and [Faster R-CNN](faster-r-cnn.qmd) additionally learns the proposal mechanism.

## Connections

The [loss note](../../study-notes/machine-learning/loss.qmd#loss-and-risk) distinguishes squared regression loss from robust alternatives.
[SSD](ssd.qmd) predicts from default boxes directly, while [DETR](detr.qmd) changes how predictions are assigned to target objects.
